text:
Marathon Petroleum rose nearly 11% over two weeks but essentially flat-lined today, down a quarter of a percent. The stock has already priced in the recent tailwinds—high crude oil prices (Brent at $114, well above the U.S. benchmark at $96), refineries running at 92.5% capacity, and tight diesel supply that Goldman Sachs expects to keep margins elevated through 2027. Today's tiny decline suggests investors are taking a breather after a strong run rather than reacting to new negative news.

The broader refining backdrop remains supportive: diesel and gasoline inventories remain tight by recent standards, and geopolitical tension in the Middle East (tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, Yemen-Houthi conflict) keeps crude prices elevated. However, the stock may also be digesting that this rally reflects expectations already baked in—refiners benefit most when crude prices rise faster than their product output prices fall, and much of that advantage appears already reflected in MPC's recent gains.
